(1) The separation of the phosphorus compounds in protein-free aqueous extract of brain and spinal cord is achieved by ion-exchange column chromatography, and the quantitative behaviour of the resin is established by the analysis of known mixtures of phosphorus compounds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ion-exchange technique is useful for separating phosphorus compounds from brain and spinal-cord extracts.
the ion-exchange technique is of considerable value in the study of the nitrogen-containing phosphorus compounds present in tissue extracts.
the method is useful for separating and identifying some of the phosphorus compounds in protein-free extracts, but it is not suitable for measuring their amounts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the separation of nitrogen-containing phosphates from each other and from other phosphates is possible, and that the method can be applied with advantage in the study of brain and spinal cord.
the separation and identification of the various phosphate esters present in brain extracts by ion-exchange column chromatography is a practicable procedure.
ion-exchange chromatographic analysis is an excellent method for the separation and estimation of phosphorus-containing nitrogen compounds.
